newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway sees oil investment at NOK 57.5 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Norway sees oil investment at NOK 57.5 bln in 1997.

text.p: Investment in the Norwegian offshore sector is expected to total 57.5 billion crowns in 1997, the highest level since 1993's record and 9.6 billion crowns higher than last year, Statistics Norway (SSB) said in a second-quarter forecast on Thursday.
In the second quarter 1996, SSB projected oil investment this year to total 33.1 billion crowns.
In its first forecast for 1998 oil spend, SSB said it expected at least 46.4 billion crowns to be invested in Norway's booming oil industry.
But, it said, this figure would likely be higher if the authorities approve proposals to develop the Oseberg South, Troll C and Jotun developments.
